## Highlights

- Correct cursor movement in tmux, with literal tabs preserved.
- Portable tab-stop initialization and resume in tmux and GNU Screen.
- Streaming OSC 52 clipboard replies with explicit completion and recovery.
- Kitty OSC 72 drag and drop messages, support detection, and a runnable example.
- Inline height changes and completed-row commits for streaming output.
- Kitty OSC 66 text sizing and image placeholder primitives.
- Extended cursor reports, UTF-8 C1 text handling, and reliable wake delivery.
- A redesigned website with new guides, examples, and contributor documentation.

Both `uncurses` and `uncurses-ratatui` use version `0.0.8`.
The adapter follows the core event changes.

## Compatibility with v0.0.7

This release includes source and behavior changes.
Review event matches, ANSI token consumers, and stored numeric input values.

### Clipboard and paste events

OSC 52 replies produce `ClipboardStart { selection }`, zero or more
`ClipboardChunk(Vec<u8>)` events, and `ClipboardEnd { complete }`.
Chunks contain raw wire bytes, normally base64. Applications decode the payload.
Chunk boundaries can split base64 groups.

`PasteEnd { complete }` also reports transfer completion.
A terminal terminator sets `complete` to `true`.
Idle recovery, explicit recovery, and input read failures produce incomplete
ends after retained payload bytes.

`EventSource` exposes clipboard and paste idle settings and explicit recovery.
The clipboard idle timeout defaults to two seconds.
Use `with_clipboard_idle_timeout(None)` to retain a reply across arbitrary delays.
`end_clipboard()` explicitly ends an incomplete reply.

Other control-string bodies remain intact across caller timeouts.
Their terminators or interrupting escape sequences determine their boundaries.

### Cursor reports

Match `Event::CursorPosition { position, page }`.
`position` contains zero-based coordinates.
`page` contains the one-based DECXCPR page number, or zero when absent.

### ANSI tokens

`ansi::text::Token` exposes `kind`, `bytes`, `width`, and `control`.
Match `TokenKind` for text, escape, and control categories.
The tokenizer recognizes 7-bit, raw C1, and UTF-8 C1 controls.
Text utilities preserve complete UTF-8 characters inside control strings.

### Keyboard and mouse values

`KeyModifiers` follows Kitty ordering across CSI keyboard forms.
`SUPER` uses bit `0x08`, and `META` uses bit `0x20`.
Xterm's Meta bit therefore maps to `SUPER`.
Use named flags when constructing or comparing modifiers.
Review serialized numeric masks.

`MouseButton::None` has discriminant zero.
Review numeric casts and stored button values.

### Windows input

`EventSource` starts with native console serialization on Windows.
Standalone callers use `set_vt_input(true)` when the console enables
`ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT`, including after `Terminal::make_raw()`.
`Program` synchronizes this setting during initialization, pause, and resume.
The setting and its accessors are Windows-only.

## Rendering and input reliability

tmux uses supported cursor sequences for long jumps.
tmux and GNU Screen use the portable tab reset even with inherited
outer-terminal variables, such as `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`.

Inline insertion accounts for wrapping, tabs, and the screen's width policy.
`Screen::resize_height()` adjusts inline height.
`Screen::commit_rows()` releases completed rows while preserving their output.
Partial writes retain unsent bytes for a later flush.

Ready input and resize events preserve pending wake notifications.
Async readers receive deadline changes and explicit transfer recovery.
Windows lifecycle operations coordinate with shared input readers.

## Examples and reference

From a checkout of this release, run examples with
`cargo run -p examples --example <name>`.
Start with `clipboard`, `drag_drop`, `inline_height`, `streaming`,
`sized_text_overlap`, or `wake`.

See the [installation guide](https://uncurses.org/docs/getting-started/installation/),
[input guides](https://uncurses.org/docs/guides/), and
[v0.0.8 API reference](https://docs.rs/uncurses/0.0.8).
